subject: Re: MedCore MSA — Security Exhibit: scope carveouts & pen-test notice window
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medcorehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medcorehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MedCore MSA: initial redlines + questions on Security Exhibit and pen-test window

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the draft MSA and security exhibit. Attached are our in-house redlines (MedCore_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) — most of our comments focus on the Security Exhibit (Audit Rights, SOC 2 assertions, and penetration testing). Two outstanding items we need clarification on before legal will proceed: 

1) Pen-test notice and scope: our security team requires a 30-day notice for non-disruptive pen tests and a hard carveout for privileged inspection beyond SOC 2 snapshots. Your exhibit currently allows a 14-day notice and broad "inspection" language — can we align on a 30-day window and define staging access as "EPHEMERAL, scoped to remediation testing only"?

2) Evidence cadence: can Redwood provide a quarterly SOC 2 summary and a dedicated S3 bucket with read-only access for evidence exports? We see reference to an evidence cadence but need specifics for our procurement acceptance criteria.

We're open to a short call tomorrow to walk through the redlines. I've copied our procurement lead, Ashley Lee, and included the SOC 2 summary for context (SOC2_summary_2028Q1.pdf).

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Counsel — Information Security
MedCore Health

Attachments: MedCore_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf), SOC2_summary_2028Q1.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-06-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedCore MSA: initial redlines + questions on Security Exhibit and pen-test window

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the redlines and the SOC 2 summary. I'm looping in Karthik (legal) and Marissa (assurance/ops) to address the two bullets you raised. Quick answers up front to keep momentum:

- Pen-test notice: we can agree to 30 days for scheduled, non-disruptive penetration tests. For emergency/incident-driven testing we expect shorter notice but will propose a defined process for "incident" exceptions.
- Evidence cadence: Redwood can provide a quarterly SOC 2 extract and we support a secure, read-only export location. Need to confirm format and retention window with Marissa.

Karthik — can you propose narrowly tailored language for the Security Exhibit that limits "inspection" to evidence exports and scoped, time-boxed access, and that provides for the 30-day scheduled pen-test notice? Marissa — can you confirm whether our evidence exports and SOC summary can be delivered to an external S3 bucket with the controls Daniel's team needs (read-only, MFA enforced, log retention 90 days)?

If we can align on language, happy to do a 30-minute call with your team on Thursday (I'll send calendar options).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-06-12T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedCore MSA: initial redlines + questions on Security Exhibit and pen-test window

Laura / Daniel —

Attached is a focused redline of the Security Exhibit (proposed_security_exhibit_redline.docx). I kept changes conservative and annotated rationale inline. Topline summary below:

1) Inspection language — replace open-ended "inspection" with the following structure:
   - Evidence Export: Redwood will provide quarterly SOC 2 extracts and supporting artifacts limited to non-production configuration artifacts and logs relevant to the SOC 2 scope.
   - Privileged Inspection: privileged or forensics-level access requires a separate mutual-approval process and is limited to agreed personnel, specific time-boxed windows, and written justification (e.g., active incident).

2) Penetration testing — we accept a 30-day notice for scheduled, non-disruptive tests. For emergency security assessments tied to an incident, Redwood may require a shorter notice to coordinate mitigations, or we will propose a jointly-operated remote test proxy to limit blast radius.

3) Staging access — carve out: "Staging environments are provided at Redwood's discretion for scoped testing; any staging access is ephemeral, time-boxed, and requires a signed access addendum."

4) Evidence delivery — Marissa, can you confirm:
   - We can deliver quarterly exports as a gzipped archive to a customer-managed S3 bucket with read-only credentials and MFA;
   - Retention: logs packaged for export will include the prior 90 days; historic artifacts beyond 90 days are available via attestation and targeted export requests.

Daniel — please confirm if that structure addresses MedCore's procurement requirements or if you need alternate artifacts (e.g., SIEM timeline exports).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: proposed_security_exhibit_redline.docx (docx)

From: Ashley Lee <procurement@medcorehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-06-13T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedCore MSA: initial redlines + questions on Security Exhibit and pen-test window

On Wed, Jun 13, 2028 at 10:03 AM PDT Ashley Lee <procurement@medcorehealth.com> wrote:

Thanks for the quick reply and the redline, Karthik. A few practical concerns from procurement/security: 

- The privileged inspection carveout is acceptable only if there is an independent auditor or cross-company checklist to trigger it — MedCore cannot accept an open bilateral approval process. Can we add an escalation path: (1) requester documents scope & justification, (2) independent third-party or Redwood security attestation verifies the request, (3) MedCore and Redwood sign-off?

- SOC 2 export format: we require exported artifacts to include file-level checksums and a manifest (hashes) for chain-of-custody.

- For pen-tests: 30 days scheduled notice is fine. One exception: we occasionally rely on coordinated third-party vendors that may need an accelerated 14-day window for tightly scoped app-layer scans; will Redwood accept conditional 14-day notice for "scoped, read-only" scans that explicitly exclude infrastructure privilege escalation?

Happy to take the call but wanted to surface these items before we meet.

Thanks,
Ashley Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
MedCore Health

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medcorehealth.com>, Ashley Lee <procurement@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-06-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedCore MSA: initial redlines + questions on Security Exhibit and pen-test window

Ashley / Daniel —

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick responses and a proposed path forward so we can close timelines: 

- Privileged inspection trigger: Redwood is willing to adopt a three-step escalation (request -> Redwood security attestation -> joint sign-off) but prefers the attestation to be performed by an independent third-party in high-sensitivity cases. We'll add language to the exhibit that requires Redwood to propose the independent attestation provider and that both parties have 7 days to object; if neither objects the provider is appointed.

- Export manifest & checksums: agreed. We'll include md5/sha256 checksums and a JSON manifest in the export bundle for chain-of-custody.

- Conditional 14-day window: Redwood can permit a conditional 14-day notice for strictly application-layer, read-only scans provided (1) scope is mutually agreed ahead of time, (2) no credentials are provided, and (3) no infrastructure or privilege escalation is requested. We'll add clear forbidden actions to the exhibit.

Next steps: Karthik will circulate an updated Security Exhibit with the three amendments above and redline the MSA where necessary. Marissa will confirm delivery mechanics and export manifest template by EOD Friday so procurement can validate. Also proposing a 30-minute alignment call Monday 2028-06-18 at 10:00am PT — please accept or propose alternatives.

If that plan works, we'll aim to finalize redlines and move to DocuSign the following week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
